name: cotton poplin
commonMistakes: skipping preshrink — cotton shrinks in the first wash
expecting drape from a crisp fabric: an A-line will stand away from the body, not flow
source: NMSU Extension G-401; SDSU Extension 4-H (good material for first time sewers); UKY Extension CT-MMB.180

name: linen
badFor: tight fitted styles that crease at every fold
commonMistakes: forgetting it wrinkles by nature and needs ironing unless treated
source: NMSU Extension G-401 (strong, durable, somewhat stiff, wrinkles and may shrink)

name: viscose / rayon
badFor: tailored or structured designs — too soft to hold the shape
commonMistakes: letting it hang off the cutting table — its own weight stretches it off grain
it is weaker when wet: wash gently
source: NMSU Extension G-401 (weaker than most fibers especially when wet, may shrink or stretch, wrinkles easily); UKY CT-MMB.180 (slippery fabrics are hardest for beginners)

name: satin
badFor: everyday hard-wearing garments — satin weaves show wear quickly
commonMistakes: choosing satin for a first project: it is slippery to cut and sew
expecting durability — the floating weave snags and shows wear
source: NMSU Extension G-401 (satin weaves are not very durable and tend to show wear quickly); UKY CT-MMB.180 (firm fabrics easier than slippery ones)

name: jersey (knit)
stretch: moderate to high — check: 10 cm folded edge stretching to ~13 cm = moderate, 15 cm+ = super stretch
badFor: our current woven blocks — knit patterns need negative ease, use woven fabric for Stitchu patterns for now
commonMistakes: sewing with a plain straight stitch — seams pop; use a narrow zigzag (1-1.5 mm)
using a regular needle — use ballpoint (75/11 light, 80/12 medium)
hemming immediately — let the garment hang 24 hours first
sliding the iron instead of pressing — stretches the fabric
source: UNL Extension NF00-415 Sewing with Knits
